I have farmed these 8 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. I never went to school but I learned from my mother and from watching what works. Six mu I plant wheat after the maize comes off, then maize again after the wheat is cut. Two mu I keep for cotton. That is my system.

For wheat on those six mu: I buy the same improved seed my neighbor Wang Dabo uses — 30 jin per mu. Before sowing I spread one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer on each mu. When the wheat turns green in March, I broadcast half a bag of urea per mu. At jointing time, another half bag. The dealer once told me this is about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, but I just know it is one and a half bags total. I irrigate four times: overwintering water so the seedlings don't freeze, green-up water, jointing water, and grain-filling water. My well can handle it. I spray three times: herbicide right after sowing, then insecticide twice in spring if I see aphids. I rotary till the maize stubble first. I expect 500 kg per mu from good land.

For maize: After the wheat comes off in June, I plant hybrid seed straight into the stubble without ploughing. No-tillage saves me diesel and two days. Everyone around here does it now. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing. When the plants reach the big trumpet stage, I side-dress one bag of urea per mu. Maize is hungry, it needs heavy feeding. I irrigate three times: after sowing if the weather is dry, at big trumpet, and during grain fill. I spray three times: herbicide once, insecticide twice for corn borer. Last year the worms were bad so I will not skip the second spray. I expect 600 kg per mu.

For cotton on two mu: I plough deep because cotton roots need loose soil. I plant improved seed, about 8 jin per mu. Cotton needs more potash than grain or the bolls rot on the plant, so I buy the fertilizer with extra potassium — one bag per mu at planting. Then I top-dress urea twice, 20 jin per mu each time. I irrigate three times and spray four times. Bollworm is the main enemy. If the weather helps I hope for 250 kg seed cotton per mu.

Why these amounts? Because this is what I did last year, and last year I did not lose money. I watch my neighbors on both sides — they do the same, and their fields looked full. I am afraid to cut back. Every jin of fertilizer costs real yuan, but a bad harvest means my family feels it in the stomach. You can waste some fertilizer and still eat. You cannot eat empty bins. My son has children to feed, so I play safe. Change is risky. What worked before will work again.
